```{r setup}
#| include: false
# All figures and numbers come from the report: its last chunk writes
# outputs/report_numbers.rds and copies its figures to figures/.
# If the report source or the shared R/ code is newer than those (or they are missing), the report is
# re-rendered first, so rendering these slides always reflects the latest report.
report <- "Quarto_report_CLIMATE-ENV-AIS.qmd"
nums   <- "outputs/report_numbers.rds"
sources <- c(report, list.files("R", full.names = TRUE))   # report + shared R code
if (!file.exists(nums) || max(file.mtime(sources)) > file.mtime(nums)) {
  message("Report changed: re-rendering ", report, " first")
  status <- system2("quarto", c("render", shQuote(report)))
  if (status != 0) stop("Report render failed; slides not updated")
}
k <- readRDS(nums)
hauls_map <- readRDS("outputs/hauls_map.rds")
pc  <- function(x, acc = 1) scales::percent(x, accuracy = acc)
pcs <- function(x, acc = 1) sub("^-", "−", scales::percent(x / 100, accuracy = acc, style_positive = "plus"))
num <- function(x, acc = 1) scales::comma(x, accuracy = acc)
pv  <- function(p) format.pval(p, digits = 1, eps = 1e-4)
mhw_top <- sort(k$mhw_cum, decreasing = TRUE)
mhw_zero <- names(k$mhw_cum)[k$mhw_cum == 0]
```

## Data

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="62%"}
```{r haul-map}

source("R/haul_map.R")   # same map as the report
haul_map(hauls_map)
```

::: {.column width="38%"}
- **MEDITS** bottom-trawl survey, 2012-2021: abundance per species and haul
- **Copernicus Marine** reanalyses at each haul: bottom temperature, salinity, chlorophyll
- **GFW AIS** apparent fishing hours, trawlers, yearly 0.1° cells, pulled with `gfwr`
- Focus on **GSA 6** (Spanish Mediterranean, Murcia to the French border)

<span class="small muted">`r num(k$n_hauls_all)` hauls in `r k$n_gsa` GSAs; `r num(k$n_hauls_gsa6)` in GSA 6 (gold). Hover over a haul for its details; scroll to zoom.</span>
:::

:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
[`r num(k$ais_hours_2012)` → `r num(k$ais_hours_2015)` h]{.big-number}

## Total fish abundance: species distribution model

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
![](figures/fig-smooths-1.png){width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
- Gaussian GAM on **log total fish abundance**, GSA 6, n = `r num(k$gam2_n)` hauls
- Bottom temperature carries most of the signal; fishing hours only marginal (p = `r pv(k$gam2_p_fishing)`)
- About **`r pc(k$gam2_dev)`** of deviance explained
- SST smooth already shrunk to zero by `select = TRUE`

::: {.caveat}
Predicted abundance 2012-2021: median **`r pcs(k$tf_change)`** per cell (`r pc(k$tf_decline)` of cells decline), partly reflecting near-zero AIS effort in 2012.
:::
:::
::::

## Red mullet: species distribution model

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
![](figures/fig-mb-smooths-1.png){width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
*Mullus barbatus* (`MULLBAR`), the group's focal species

- **Zeros kept:** caught in `r num(k$mb_present)` of `r num(k$mb_hauls)` GSA 6 hauls (`r pc(k$mb_present / k$mb_hauls)`)
- **Tweedie GAM** (log link): handles zeros and skewed catches, predicts N/km² directly
- **Depth added:** deviance explained **`r pc(k$mb_dev_env)` → `r pc(k$mb_dev_depth)`**, AIC −`r num(k$mb_aic_drop)`
- Density high to ~200 m, then falls steeply; ↑ with bottom temperature, ↓ with chlorophyll

::: {.caveat}
The fishing-hours smooth peaks at zero effort: likely **confounding** (trawlers target mullet grounds), so treated as a nuisance covariate.
:::
:::
::::

## Red mullet: habitat change 2015-2021

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
![](figures/fig-mb-change-1.png){width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
June predictions on the Copernicus hindcast grid, within the sampled depth range; change computed after the AIS ramp-up

[`r pcs(k$mb_change_env)`]{.big-number}
[median change per cell with effort held constant (`r pcs(k$mb_change_full)` with the full model)]{.big-label}

[`r pc(k$mb_decline_env)`]{.big-number}
[of `r num(k$mb_cells)` cells decline with effort held constant (range `r pcs(k$mb_min_env)` to `r pcs(k$mb_max_env)`)]{.big-label}

::: {.caveat}
Mean bottom temperature is similar in 2015 and 2021, so the decline is **not simply warming**. Driver not yet identified.
:::
:::
::::

## Red mullet in two areas: spatio-temporal model {.section-break background-color="#062d4a"}

GSA 6 and the Adriatic (GSAs 17-18), 2014-2021 · report Section 2c

## Spatio-temporal model: data and structure

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
- **Biomass** (kg/km²), MEDITS 2014-2021: `r num(k$grp_hauls[["GSA 6"]])` hauls in GSA 6, `r num(k$grp_hauls[["GSAs 17-18"]])` in the Adriatic
- **sdmTMB**, Tweedie, fitted separately in each area:

<p style="text-align:center; margin:0.8em 0;">log(biomass) = **bottom temp. + depth** + **ω** (spatial) + **ε** (AR(1) by year)</p>

- Both models converge; observed vs fitted r = `r num(k$grp_cor[["GSA 6"]], 0.01)` (GSA 6) and `r num(k$grp_cor[["GSAs 17-18"]], 0.01)` (Adriatic)
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
| | GSA 6 | GSAs 17-18 |
|---|---|---|
| Per +100 m depth | −`r pc(k$grp_depth_drop[["GSA 6"]])` | −`r pc(k$grp_depth_drop[["GSAs 17-18"]])` |
| Per +1 °C bottom temp. | `r pcs(100 * k$grp_temp$per_c[1])` | `r pcs(100 * k$grp_temp$per_c[2])` |
| Largest \|ε\| | `r num(k$grp_eps_max[["GSA 6"]], 0.1)` | `r num(k$grp_eps_max[["GSAs 17-18"]], 0.1)` |
:::
::::

## Bottom temperature: two areas compared

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
![](figures/fig-grp-temp-1.png){width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
[`r pcs(100 * k$grp_temp$per_c[2])`]{.big-number}
[biomass per +1 °C in the Adriatic (95% CI `r pcs(100 * k$grp_temp$lo[2])` to `r pcs(100 * k$grp_temp$hi[2])`)]{.big-label}

[`r pcs(100 * k$grp_temp$per_c[1])`]{.big-number}
[per +1 °C in GSA 6 (95% CI `r pcs(100 * k$grp_temp$lo[1])` to `r pcs(100 * k$grp_temp$hi[1])`): not significant]{.big-label}

::: {.caveat}
**Discussion point:** GSA 6 hauls span a narrow range of bottom temperatures, so the effect is poorly constrained there and depth dominates.
:::

:::: {.columns}

![](figures/fig-grp-index-1.png){width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
[`r pcs(100 * k$grp_idx_6_change)`]{.big-number}
[GSA 6, 2015 → 2021 (Tweedie GAM: `r pcs(k$grp_gam_change)` in density)]{.big-label}

[`r pc(k$grp_idx_1718_rng[1])` to `r pc(k$grp_idx_1718_rng[2])`]{.big-number}
[The Adriatic index fluctuates more, between `r pc(k$grp_idx_1718_rng[1])` and `r pc(k$grp_idx_1718_rng[2])` of its 2014-2021 mean]{.big-label}

::: {.caveat}
**Discussion point:** each area peaks in its **least-sampled year** (GSA 6 2020: `r k$grp_thin_6` hauls; Adriatic 2017: `r k$grp_thin_1718`). Needs index standard errors.
:::

## Habitat suitability index (HSI)

![](figures/fig-grp-hsi-1.png){width="100%" fig-align="center"}

[Fixed effects (depth + bottom temperature) rescaled to 0-1 within each area. Highest on the shallow inner shelf; in the Adriatic, the northern basin scores high almost everywhere.]{.small .muted}

## Change in habitat suitability, 2014 to 2021

![](figures/fig-grp-perc-1.png){width="80%" fig-align="center"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- GSA 6: median **`r pcs(k$grp_perc_med[["GSA 6"]], 0.1)`**, almost no change
- Adriatic: median **`r pcs(k$grp_perc_med[["GSAs 17-18"]], 0.1)`**; `r pc(k$grp_hsi_lower[["GSAs 17-18"]])` of cells lose suitability, mainly the northern basin
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.caveat}
**Discussion point:** the % change explodes where HSI ≈ 0 (up to `r pcs(k$grp_perc_max_6)` in one GSA 6 cell): prefer the **HSI difference** or a **2014-2021 trend**.
:::
:::
::::

## Overlap between red mullet and trawling

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
![](data/group/correlation_map_2700.jpeg){width="86%" fig-align="center"}
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
Local correlation between red mullet and **GFW trawling effort**, by year

- **Red**: trawling concentrated where red mullet is abundant
- GSA 6: mostly negative, positive patches on the outer shelf
- Adriatic: a positive band through the north-western and central basin every year

::: {.caveat}
**Discussion point:** correlations near ±1 are common in small windows: add a **significance test** or a **whole-area overlap measure**.
:::
:::
::::

## Do the fleets fish the same grounds?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="56%"}
![](figures/fig-grp-core-1.png){width="100%"}

[Core grounds (cells with 80% of hours): blue-grey in both types of summer, red strong only, dark blue weak only.]{.small .muted}
:::
::: {.column width="44%"}
::: {.small}
| | GSA 6 | Adriatic |
|---|---|---|
| Overlap D, strong vs weak | `r subset(k$grp_overlap_tab, Area == "GSA 6" & Pair == "Strong vs weak")[["Schoener's D"]]` | `r subset(k$grp_overlap_tab, Area == "GSAs 17-18" & Pair == "Strong vs weak")[["Schoener's D"]]` |
| Overlap D, same type | `r paste(subset(k$grp_overlap_tab, Area == "GSA 6" & Pair != "Strong vs weak")[["Schoener's D"]], collapse = ", ")` | `r paste(subset(k$grp_overlap_tab, Area == "GSAs 17-18" & Pair != "Strong vs weak")[["Schoener's D"]], collapse = ", ")` |
| Centre shift | `r subset(k$grp_overlap_tab, Area == "GSA 6" & Pair == "Strong vs weak")[["Centre-of-gravity shift (km)"]]` km | `r subset(k$grp_overlap_tab, Area == "GSAs 17-18" & Pair == "Strong vs weak")[["Centre-of-gravity shift (km)"]]` km |
| Effort on red mullet hotspots | `r with(subset(k$grp_hab, region == "GSA 6"), paste(scales::percent(hot[class == "strong"], 1), "/", scales::percent(hot[class == "weak"], 1)))` | `r with(subset(k$grp_hab, region == "GSAs 17-18"), paste(scales::percent(hot[class == "strong"], 1), "/", scales::percent(hot[class == "weak"], 1)))` |
:::

**Same grounds** in strong and weak heatwave summers: overlap as high as between two summers of the same type (D: 1 = identical effort distribution).
:::
::::

## Heatwaves and red mullet biomass across years

![](figures/fig-grp-annual-1.png){width="72%" fig-align="center"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%" .small}
**Adriatic:** biomass drops in the two strongest heatwave summers (2015, 2018), recovers the year after; overall ρ = `r round(subset(k$grp_annual_cor, region == "GSAs 17-18")$same, 2)`
:::
::: {.column width="30%" .small}
**GSA 6:** the opposite, its strongest heatwave summers are among its higher-biomass years (ρ = `r round(subset(k$grp_annual_cor, region == "GSA 6")$same, 2)`)
:::
::: {.column width="36%"}
::: {.caveat}
**Discussion point:** eight years per area, two areas in opposite directions: a hypothesis to test, not a result.
:::
:::
::::

## Heatwaves and red mullet biomass within years

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="64%"}
![](figures/fig-grp-rel-gam-1.png){width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="36%"}
Year-specific deviation of predicted biomass (ε) in each cell, against heatwaves and trawling, with depth, latitude and year in the model

- **GSA 6:** small effects
- **Adriatic:** not monotonic, a dip at moderate heat, higher biomass in the hottest cells
- **No trawling effect** in either area
- Does not reproduce the annual dips
:::

## Climate-fisheries vulnerability index

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
![](figures/fig-cfvi-1.png){width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
Mean of three 0-1 scores: **heatwave exposure + habitat loss + fishing pressure**

- Hotspots off Cap de Creus-Roses and nearshore off the Ebro and Valencia

::: {.caveat}
- Exposure from 2021 only: **`r pc(k$cfvi_exp_zero)`** of cells score exactly 0
- Pressure very skewed: median score `r num(k$cfvi_press_med, 0.01)`

**Better:** 2015-2021 mean exposure, log effort, test the weights
:::
:::
::::

## Next steps

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Fix in the existing pipeline**

1. **AIS ramp-up:** start in 2015 or normalise effort per vessel
2. **Extrapolation:** predict in the survey months and sampled depth range
3. **Zeros:** same treatment of unmatched effort in fitting, prediction and averaging
4. **Index design:** align time windows, test transformation and weights
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Red mullet**

- Identify which environmental term drives the 2015-2021 decline
- Check it against the observed MEDITS trend
- Feed red mullet habitat change into the vulnerability index in place of total fish
- Spatio-temporal model: index standard errors, cross-validation
- Heatwaves: effort on heatwave days vs other days; heatwave intensity as a model covariate
:::
::::

## Red mullet and depth

![](figures/fig-mb-depth-1.png){width="100%"}

[Occurrence and mean density by haul depth, GSA 6 MEDITS hauls 2012-2021]{.small .muted}
